svg.title: B22 / NIF ODYSSEY — Comparative Nitrogen-Fixation Evolution engineering mission profile
svg.desc: B22, NIF ODYSSEY — Comparative Nitrogen-Fixation Evolution. Original project: Developing a model system using Azotobacter vinelandii to investigate the evolution of nitrogen fixation. Session B: Earth & Environmental Engineering. Scientific question: Which evolutionary and regulatory constraints explain conservation/divergence of nitrogen-fixation systems in available genomes? Testable hypothesis: Metal availability and energetic allocation may explain distinct nitrogenase-system histories; phylogenetic signal and genomic context should outperform gene-presence explanations alone.. svg.text: Developing a model system using Azotobacter vinelandii to investigate the evolution of nitrogen fixation
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Develop a computational model system around existing Azotobacter vinelandii
genome, expression and metabolic evidence. Compare nitrogenase lineages,
regulation and energetic tradeoffs through retrospective analysis and
simulation. Preserve the evolutionary question without constructing,
selecting or experimentally adapting strains; computational ancestral
inference is clearly distinguished from validated historical enzyme
Which evolutionary and regulatory constraints explain
conservation/divergence of nitrogen-fixation systems in available genomes?
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
Metal availability and energetic allocation may explain distinct
nitrogenase-system histories; phylogenetic signal and genomic context should
Presence of homologs does not prove a functional nitrogenase system.
Substitution models and alignment choices affect ancestral inference.
Steady-state metabolic bounds are scenario assumptions and need experimental
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
Horizontal transfer, incomplete genomes and deep-time saturation complicate
ancestry. Constraint-based fluxes are feasible states rather than measured
rates; inferred sequences cannot prove ancestral activity.
COUNTS OF RECORDS · NO COMPLETION SCORES
TRACEABILITY / IDs THAT STAY WITH THE WORK
Execution evidence is required before case closure.

A question becomes a model. A model earns evidence.
NASA-inspired mission names are creative identifiers. This profile describes research design; it claims no NASA approval or flight qualification.
